published.protocol: Tmax = 2.4 n s, 10 seeds, all 100 X instances

note: 30 of the 100 X instances (every ~3rd by size, n = 100 to 1000), one seed, at 10% of the published time budget (0.24·n s instead of 2.4·n s), because the shared CPU allows ~5 cores across ten projects. The full race (PyVRP and OR-Tools on CPU, cuOpt on one L4 GPU) gives a mean gap to best-known of 0.49% (CPU racers alone 0.60%; cuOpt wins 10 of 30 instances); 2 instances hit the best-known solution exactly and 18 are within 0.5%. OR-Tools alone averages 7.96% and found no feasible plan within budget on 4 tight-capacity instance(s). NVIDIA cuOpt on one L4 GPU, same budget, averages 0.99% over 30 instances (objective setting chosen on X-n101 only: default+k1; cuOpt minimises fleet size before distance by default). At the full published budget on the 6 smallest instances PyVRP averages 0.05% (the same instances at 10% budget: 0.31%), against the published 0.22% (PyVRP) and 0.11% (HGS-CVRP) over all 100 instances and 10 seeds. Verdict rule: reached = within the published PyVRP gap; close = within about 2x of it or matching it at full budget on a subset; otherwise not reached.
short: 30 CVRPLIB X instances at 10% of the published time: the open-source race (CPU + GPU) averages 0.49% from best-known (published state of the art at full time: 0.11–0.22%).
